draft.title: Kinds of essay topics
card: Theme topic
It asks about an idea the text explores, such as power or belonging. Your focus is how the whole text develops that idea.
Character topic
It asks about a person in the text. Your focus is what the character wants, how they change and what they stand for.
Quotation topic
It gives words from the text and asks you to respond to them. Your focus is what the words claim, then how the whole text supports or tests that claim.
Construction topic
It asks how the writer builds meaning through choices such as structure, setting, point of view or language. Your focus is those choices and their effects.
draft.remember: First name the kind of topic, then choose a focus that fits it.

a.q: A topic asks: How does the writer use a shifting point of view to shape the reader's response? What kind of topic is this?
opts: A construction topic
A theme topic
A character topic
A quotation topic
a.why: The topic asks how the writer builds meaning through a choice, point of view. That is a construction topic. It is not a character topic, even though point of view often involves characters, because the focus is the writer's method.
a.clue: Look at what the topic asks you to explain: the idea, or the writer's method?

b.q: Dev has a topic that gives a line spoken by a character and asks whether the text agrees with it. What should his essay focus on?
opts: What the line claims, and how the whole text treats it
Only the character who speaks the line and their motives
Only the language techniques used inside the line itself
A summary of the scenes before and after the line
b.why: A quotation topic asks you to respond to the claim in the words, using the whole text. Focusing only on the speaker treats it as a character topic, and that leaves the claim untested.
b.clue: The topic asks whether the text agrees, so think about the whole text.

b.best: What the line claims, and how the whole text treats it

problems.detail: The clue says 'think about the whole text', and only the right option contains 'the whole text'. A student can match the words without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card and both answers are accurate. The only problem is that question b's clue repeats the phrase 'the whole text' from the right option, which gives the answer away.
